title: BeaconRetail Edge fallthrough & streaming backpressure demo
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked BeaconRetail through an edge-case focused demo: long 200k+ token contexts, sustained high TPS bursts, streaming backpressure scenarios and graceful fallthroughs to cheaper variants. Security questions about KMS, audit logs and VPC were raised. Agreed next steps: run a short POC with BeaconRetail test corpus, share security docs and benchmark instructions, and schedule a follow-up to review pilot results.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-02 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Dana Morales (BeaconRetail Eng Manager), Samir Patel (BeaconRetail Platform), Evelyn Cho (BeaconRetail ML), Rajiv Menon (BeaconRetail Security)

Summary (auto): demo focused on failure modes under long-context + high TPS, showed fallthrough policies and streaming fallbacks, discussed security and pilot plan.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, and then priya will jump into the demo.
[00:17] Dana (BeaconRetail): hi all, dana here. we've got a pretty gnarly workload — long chat histories, shopping session traces, and spikes during promos that hit us with thousands of requests per second for short windows.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood): great, that's exactly what we wanted to show. i'm going to start with an overview of how redwood's runtime manages extremely long contexts — like 50k to 200k tokens — and then show what happens under sustained TPS bursts when streaming responses start to back up.
[01:05] Samir (BeaconRetail): quick clarifying Q — when you say 200k tokens, is that full dense context or do you mean a combination of KV cache + prefix storage?
[01:20] Priya (Redwood): good callout. we generally split between prefix context (kept in memory) and a compressed KV cache for prior activations. real world is mixed; in the demo i'll replicate both: long prefix + large KV window and then intentionally force eviction to show truncation behavior.
[01:45] Liam (Redwood): small note, some of the labels in the metrics UI you see are auto-normalized; the transcript might show "K V cache" as separate words sometimes, the console shows it as KVCache.
[02:05] Evelyn (BeaconRetail): we've run into streaming stalls where partial responses hang and clients retry, which multiplies load. curious to see how your fallback handles that.
[02:22] Priya (Redwood): yep — we'll demonstrate backpressure scenarios and our recommended client-side retry policies plus server-side shedding. first up, live console.
[03:10] [screen share starts] Priya (Redwood): here is the route config for the demo app — long-context route pinned to model-redwood-xxl-q8, streaming enabled, kv_cache set to 300k entries (simulated), and a fallback policy to model-redwood-xxl-q4 for cost-tier fallback and model-variant mismatch.
[03:40] Dana (BeaconRetail): is that a hard fallback after X queue depth, or is it per-request?
[03:50] Priya (Redwood): it can be policy-driven. in this demo we've set thresholds: if queue latency > 350ms for more than 3s we route new requests to the q4 variant. if memory pressure on the node triggers kv eviction we strip old prefixes and signal a partial-context fallback.
[04:25] [00:04:25] Jordan (Redwood): note — these thresholds are examples; for your workload we usually tune based on percentiles you care about — p50/p95 of response time and successful completion rate.
[04:48] [00:04:48] Priya (Redwood): launching a synthetic workload: 1k sustained TPS for 45 seconds, then a promo spike to 6k TPS for 30s. payloads include 10k token user histories for baseline and 100k token histories for stress.
[05:12] [00:05:12] Priya (Redwood): during baseline you can see GPU utilization is stable, streaming latencies around 120ms per token. switching to the 6k spike now — watch the per-route queues.
[06:00] [00:06:00] Samir (BeaconRetail): i see queue depth climbing and a backlog of partial streams in the console. what happens to clients mid-stream?
[06:12] Priya (Redwood): good question — we have two layers: 1) server-side shedders that start routing new requests to cheaper variants or to a standby region; 2) graceful truncation of KV/prefix for in-flight requests if necessary, and then we either continue the stream with partial context or close the stream with an explicit fallback token so clients can retry against a non-streamed endpoint.
[06:45] Rajiv (BeaconRetail): from a security perspective, when you migrate a request to a different model pool or region, is data encrypted at rest and do you preserve audit context?
[06:58] Priya (Redwood): yes — we keep request-level metadata and audit logs tied to the original request_id. when crossing regions or pools we re-encrypt using the configured KMS. our private deployment supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and we can preserve tenant separation in Dedicated pools.
[07:20] [screen note] Priya (Redwood): starting a different scenario: long-context KV eviction — we'll artificially reduce KV capacity to force truncation and show the degradation profile for downstream answers.
[07:48] [00:07:48] Priya (Redwood): you can see how the model begins to hallucinate slightly more as older context is evicted; our optimize product flags regressions relative to a golden prompt set and raises alerts when quality drops beyond your threshold.
[08:20] Dana (BeaconRetail): that's valuable — can the alert trigger an auto-rollback to cached shorter-history responses if quality drops too much?
[08:32] Priya (Redwood): absolutely; rollbacks can be automatic with a canary policy: if quality falls below X for the canary sample, we switch the route to a version pinned to a deterministic shorter history policy.
[08:55] [00:08:55] Liam (Redwood): showing the console trace now — per-token latency, per-model cost, and a timeline of routing decisions. note the grading line that shows when the fallback kicked in.
[09:20] [00:09:20] Jordan (Redwood): quick interruption — Samir, you mentioned clients retrying. what client library are you using?
[09:30] Samir (BeaconRetail): custom node service with our own retry logic, exponential backoff and jitter, but we lack strong telemetry to correlate retries with server-side shedding.
[09:45] Jordan (Redwood): perfect use-case for our tracing hooks — token-level and request-level traces can be forwarded to your existing observability stack. we also add headers that indicate if the request was fallthrough or truncated.
[10:08] [00:10:08] Priya (Redwood): moving to streaming backpressure demonstration: first run without any fallback — you'll see the number of partial streams blow up and downstream clients starting to timeout.
[10:35] [00:10:35] demo log: baseline -> spike -> no fallback: partial streams accumulated, many clients timed out after their 10s socket timeout, causing retries and a retry storm.
[11:02] Samir (BeaconRetail): that's exactly our past incident — retries multiplied the load. how do you prevent the retry storm at the client side?
[11:15] Priya (Redwood): we recommend the following client patterns: 1) idempotency keys for user-facing operations, 2) retry-after headers from server when shedding, 3) circuit-breaker on the client side tuned to server-specified thresholds, and 4) hybrid: attempt streaming for up to N tokens then switch to polling for final result.
[11:45] Rajiv (BeaconRetail): also need to understand data residency if you shift to a fallback in another region. do you surface that to the app?
[11:58] Priya (Redwood): yes, fallbacks are policy-aware for data residency. you can block cross-region fallback for regulated workloads; otherwise we log region of execution in audit logs. the console shows an execution-region tag per request.
[12:30] [00:12:30] Jordan (Redwood): now we'll run the shedding policy demo where new requests get routed to a cheaper quantized variant as queue depth increases, and in-flight streams are signaled to end with a fallback condition so clients don't continue to stream indefinitely.
[12:58] demo: shedding policy enabled -> spike -> new requests hit q4 variant, in-flight streams ended with finite token sentinel.
[13:20] Evelyn (BeaconRetail): when in-flight streams end early, do you provide a reason code so the frontend can show a user message?
[13:32] Priya (Redwood): yes — we have structured exit codes: REASON=partial_context_eviction, REASON=shed_to_variant, REASON=timeout_fallback; these are in the response headers and in the trace. sometimes downstream systems mis-parse them though — we saw "shed" show up as "shot" in old logs, it's imperfect.
[14:05] [00:14:05] Priya (Redwood): switching gears — now a demo of the optimize suggestions. given your traffic pattern, optimize will recommend batching windows and per-route quantization profiles; here's a suggested config that would lower token cost by ~27% while keeping p95 latency within your 450ms SLO.
[14:40] Dana (BeaconRetail): what's the risk of quality degradation with that 27% win?
[14:50] Priya (Redwood): we ran it across your sample eval set and quality delta was <2% on the metrics you provided (intent preservation and slot accuracy). optimize flags which prompts are sensitive and suggests keeping those routes on full precision.
[15:10] [00:15:10] demo log: apply suggested config to canary route.
[15:30] [00:15:30] Priya (Redwood): next scenario: long-context handoff across sessions. we'll simulate a user that reconnects after network drop — we preserve a short summary as a compacted prefix to avoid re-sending 80k tokens while keeping conversational continuity.
[16:00] Samir (BeaconRetail): what's your approach to summarization for state preservation? automated abstractive summarization or deterministic chunk hashing?
[16:12] Priya (Redwood): we offer both: deterministic fingerprint-based checkpoints for legal auditability and abstractive summaries for cost savings. you can choose per-route.
[16:35] Rajiv (BeaconRetail): audit logs must show original messages if legal requires it; can you keep those behind customer KMS?
[16:48] Priya (Redwood): yes, redwood supports customer-managed keys; logs can be encrypted and retained per your retention policy. also we can provide an immutable timeline export for compliance reviews.
[17:10] [00:17:10] Jordan (Redwood): quick pivot to procurement question — Dana, any timeline constraints for proof-of-concept?
[17:20] Dana (BeaconRetail): we want a pilot live before holiday promo season — so ideally start pilot in two weeks and run for two weeks to capture a spike window.
[17:33] Jordan (Redwood): great — that's doable. we'll provision a small dedicated capacity pool and run synthetic promos in parallel with your staging traffic.
[17:45] [00:17:45] Priya (Redwood): demo: running a worst-case scenario — simultaneous 10k TPS with mixed 100k token histories. console shows fallback to standby region and aggressive shedding.
[18:10] [00:18:10] demo log: standby region accepted new requests at lower cost tier, some requests returned with fallback reason, overall availability stayed at 98% during the simulated spike.
[18:35] Evelyn (BeaconRetail): 98% is okay but we need to quantify business impact — how many sessions ended with degraded answers vs. full success?
[18:45] Priya (Redwood): in this run, about 12% of sessions were truncated and 6% were routed to the cheaper variant with measurable drop in slot-filling accuracy. we logged all of those for analysis.
[19:05] Samir (BeaconRetail): can we set a policy that for VIP customers we never fallback to cheaper variant and instead queue or spin up extra capacity?
[19:18] Priya (Redwood): yes — per-tenant and per-cusotmer routing policies support VIP rules; you can set priority and allow overage bursting for specific subtenants.
[19:36] [00:19:36] Liam (Redwood): small spelling note in the transcript — sometimes "canary" got transcribed as "cannery" in the demo captions.
[19:50] [00:19:50] Jordan (Redwood): security focused question now — Rajiv?
[19:55] Rajiv (BeaconRetail): yes — we need SOC2 + ISO artifacts, and we want to validate network isolation in Dedicated pools. also curious about your logging retention options and if we can push logs into our S3 buckets encrypted with our KMS.
[20:15] Priya (Redwood): we can push audit logs via syslog/forwarder to your S3. retention and encryption are configurable, and on private deployments you control the KMS. we'll include our SOC2 package and a network diagram in the security pack.
[20:40] [00:20:40] Jordan (Redwood): switching to a short troubleshooting demo: timeouts and partial stream reconciliation.
[20:55] Priya (Redwood): reproducing a client timeout: we set client socket to 8 seconds, streaming stays idle for 9s due to token generation stall — client retries. server rejects with a throttling header but sometimes clients immediately retry without reading the header.
[21:20] Samir (BeaconRetail): that's the problem we've seen. how do you ensure clients respect retry-after?
[21:30] Priya (Redwood): for web clients we recommend an SDK that honors retry-after and a backoff jitter. we also surface server-side Retry-After seconds and a numeric reason code. if your client can't be patched quickly we can insert an edge proxy that rewrites the header for legacy behavior.
[21:55] [00:21:55] demo log: enabled edge-proxy -> legacy clients honor Retry-After -> retry storms reduced by 82%.
[22:20] Dana (BeaconRetail): can the edge proxy be self-hosted?
[22:30] Jordan (Redwood): yes — we provide a small proxy image you can run in your k8s cluster that forwards metrics and rewrites headers where needed.
[22:48] [00:22:48] Priya (Redwood): final demo bit — KV-cache cold-start penalties. we show a cold host coming online, first requests hit cache miss and latency spikes; subsequently KV warms and latency drops.
[23:15] [00:23:15] demo log: cold start -> 1.8x latency spike for first 200 requests -> warmed in ~45s with prefetcher enabled.
[23:40] Evelyn (BeaconRetail): does prefetching add cost?
[23:52] Priya (Redwood): minimal; it's targeted prefetch of top-k entries for predicted sessions based on your traffic shape. often the cost is less than the business impact of a slow user flow.
[24:10] [00:24:10] Jordan (Redwood): time check — about half hour in, would you like to dig deeper into any scenario?
[24:20] Dana (BeaconRetail): let's go deeper on pilot plan — steps we need to run a realistic test with our staging.
[24:35] Jordan (Redwood): we'll need traffic samples, a staging service account, and a quick mapping of routes you care about. priya will share the exact probing scripts.
[24:48] Priya (Redwood): i'll also include a set of canary prompt templates so your ML folks can map quality metrics back to business metrics.
[25:10] [00:25:10] Samir (BeaconRetail): security — we'll need to validate network peering and that kerberos / sso flows are possible for the staging env.
[25:25] Rajiv (BeaconRetail): also include a list of minimal logs we need to keep for audit — want to see format before agreeing to retention.
[25:40] Priya (Redwood): yes we'll include log schemas and retention options in the security pack.
[26:05] [00:26:05] demo: small run of regional fallback with data-residency block enabled — nothing crossed region, fallback stayed in-region to cheaper quant variant.
[26:30] Dana (BeaconRetail): perfect. what about billing during the pilot if we hit a massive promo spike?
[26:45] Jordan (Redwood): for pilots we put a usage cap or alerting thresholds and can offer a temporary overage buffer for a funded pilot. we'll share examples in the pricing sketch.
[27:10] [00:27:10] Priya (Redwood): last technical point — when streaming is torn down and we resume on a different model, you may see minor tokenization differences; we tag those and provide a reconciliation API to stitch partial outputs into a single canonical response.
[27:40] Evelyn (BeaconRetail): stitch API — will that keep timestamps and original tokens for audit?
[27:55] Priya (Redwood): yes, stitches preserve token offsets and original timestamps, and are linkable to audit logs.
[28:20] [00:28:20] Jordan (Redwood): open floor for any remaining Qs.
[28:28] Dana (BeaconRetail): a couple questions — 1) can you show cost delta if we force no fallbacks for VIP customers, 2) what's the SLA for Dedicated behind a VPC?
[28:42] Priya (Redwood): 1) cost delta depends on burst shape; we can model it — quick estimate is +40-70% during heavy spikes because you either pay for reserved burst or suffer queueing. 2) Dedicated SLA depends on tier — standard dedicated is 99.9% with defined latency SLOs; premium gets higher. we'll include exact numbers.
[29:10] [00:29:10] Jordan (Redwood): wrapping up, we'll send the security pack, a sample pilot plan, and our suggested config for your routes.
[29:22] [00:29:22] Dana (BeaconRetail): thanks — please also include a short runbook we can give to our on-call team for promo spikes.
[29:34] Jordan (Redwood): will do. any last minute items?
[29:40] Samir (BeaconRetail): can you run one quick mini-benchmark with our redacted logs and share the output in CSV?
[29:50] Priya (Redwood): yes — once we get logs we can run a tailored benchmark.
[30:05] [00:30:05] quick aside: pricing sketch displayed (not shared in transcript).
[30:20] [00:30:20] Jordan (Redwood): final notes — we'll follow up with calendar invite for pilot kickoff and include obligations for both sides. thanks everyone.
[30:35] [recording ends]

Post-call notes: participants requested security artifacts and an environment checklist. agreed to start pilot in two weeks. transcript contains some mis-transcriptions of technical terms (e.g., KV -> K V, canary -> cannery) and some overlapping talk; raw audio will be attached in CRM.
